title: LLM Function Calling Tool Definitions
description: OpenRouter-compatible tool schemas for browser automation agent. Used for command interpretation via LLM function calling (claude-3.5-sonnet).

function.name: navigate
function.description: Navigate the browser to a specified URL. Use this when the user wants to go to a website or load a new page.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Must include protocol (http:// or https://). Examples: 'https://google.com', 'http://example.com'

wait_for.description: When to consider navigation complete. 'load' waits for full page load, 'domcontentloaded' waits for DOM ready, 'networkidle' waits for no network activity.

function.name: click
function.description: Click an element on the current page. Use this when the user wants to click a button, link, or other clickable element.

element_description.description: Human-readable description of the element to click. Examples: 'login button', 'first search result', 'submit form button'. This will be used for multi-strategy element finding.

selector.description: Optional CSS selector or XPath for precise targeting. If provided, takes precedence over element_description.

text.description: Optional exact or partial text content of the element to click. Example: 'Sign In', 'Learn More'.

role.description: Optional ARIA role of the element to narrow search.

function.name: type_text
function.description: Type text into an input field on the current page. Use this when the user wants to enter text, fill a form field, or search.

element_description.description: Human-readable description of the input field. Examples: 'email input', 'search box', 'username field'.

text.description: The text to type into the field.

selector.description: Optional CSS selector for precise targeting of the input field.

clear_first.description: Whether to clear existing text before typing. Default true.

press_enter.description: Whether to press Enter after typing (e.g., for search submission). Default false.

function.name: extract_information
function.description: Extract information from the current page. Use this when the user asks questions like 'What is...', 'How many...', 'Find...', 'List...'.

extraction_type.description: Type of extraction: 'text' for single text content, 'attribute' for element attributes (href, src), 'count' for counting elements, 'list' for multiple items.

target_description.description: Description of what to extract. Examples: 'page title', 'all email addresses', 'product price', 'main headings'.

selector.description: Optional CSS selector for the target element(s).

attribute_name.description: Required if extraction_type is 'attribute'. The attribute to extract (e.g., 'href', 'src', 'alt').

limit.description: For 'list' extraction, maximum number of items to return. Default 10.

function.name: scroll
function.description: Scroll the page or a specific element. Use this when the user wants to scroll down, scroll up, or scroll to an element.

direction.description: Scroll direction: 'down' scrolls down one page, 'up' scrolls up one page, 'to_element' scrolls to bring an element into view.

element_description.description: Required if direction is 'to_element'. Description of the element to scroll to.

pixels.description: Optional number of pixels to scroll. If not provided, scrolls one viewport height.

function.name: configure_timeout
function.description: Change the page load timeout setting for the current session. Use this when the user types '/timeout N' or asks to change timeout settings.

timeout_seconds.description: New timeout value in seconds. Valid range: 1-300 seconds.

url_validation.description: URLs must include http:// or https:// protocol

element_description_validation.description: Element descriptions should be clear, specific, and human-readable

confidence_thresholds.description: Confidence calculation based on parameter completeness
confidence_thresholds.high_confidence: selector OR (element_description AND text) OR (element_description AND role)

response_format.description: LLM should respond with function calls in OpenRouter format

multi_step_handling.description: For compound commands, LLM should return multiple tool calls in sequence
multi_step_handling.example_command: Go to amazon.com, search for 'laptop', and show the first 3 results

notes: This schema is used by INFRA-004 (OpenRouter LLM client) and US1-002 (LLM integration)
Tool definitions follow OpenAI/OpenRouter function calling format
Element descriptions are intentionally flexible to support natural language interpretation
Confidence evaluation (US5-001) analyzes parameter completeness from these tool calls
